item.title: Colombia's government sparks backlash with museum art purge
item.description: Colombia's new president vows a "cultural counterrevolution" against wokeness, and his removal of 47 artworks from a national museum is sparking protests and fears of government censorship.

item.title: Polls close in Israel with opposition ahead but no clear winner
item.description: Voting in Israel has ended and exit polls suggest most Israelis have voted against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. But the center-right opposition may struggle to build a governing coalition.
item.content:encoded: Voting in Israel has ended and exit polls suggest most Israelis have voted against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. But the center-right opposition may struggle to build a governing coalition.

item.title: Hotel owner in the Andes organizes his community to watch for fires
item.description: In the Peruvian Andes, a hotel owner is helping his community prepare for wildfires. It's a role that's put him and other local businesses at the forefront of helping Peru respond to El Nino threats.

item.title: For Milwaukee Brewers 1st baseman Jake Bauers, this World Series is extra special
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers first baseman Jake Bauers almost didn't play in this World Series. In 2024, he came close to quitting baseball to become a stay-at-home dad. But he needed health benefits.

item.title: Oxford Street bans traffic
item.description: London is pedestrianizing its version of Fifth Avenue. Cars, taxis, buses and even bicycles are now banned from Oxford Street.

item.title: How internet culture and franchise twists defined this year's horror movies
item.description: Horror critic and director Rebekah McKendry tells NPR's Juana Summers how internet culture led to some of this year's biggest horror movies, and shares some titles that may have gone under the radar.

item.title: Some people with meat allergies from alpha-gal syndrome turn to exotic alternatives
item.description: People with alpha-gal syndrome can have allergic reactions to meat from mammals. Many of those affected change their diets to eat other proteins.
